record.original_question: Let d tend to infinity. Is there a function g(d)=o(d/log d) such that every graphing G of maximum degree at most d admits a measurable partition of its vertex space I=[0,1] into A∪B for which every vertex x has nearly balanced degrees into A and B, meaning the two degrees differ by at most g(d)?

evidence.quote: Problem 3.2. Let d → ∞. Prove that there is g(d) = o(d/ log d) such that any graphing G of maximum degree at most d admits a measurable partition I = A ∪ B such that for every vertex x is (A, B)-balanced, meaning that its degrees into A and into B differ by at most g(d).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A graphing is a graph $G$ whose vertex set is the unit interval $I=[0,1]$ equipped with the Lebesgue measure, whose edge set is a Borel subset of $I\times I$, and whose adjacency is generated by finitely many measurable, measure-preserving, almost-everywhere involutions of $I$, so that for almost every $x\in I$ the degree $\deg_G(x)$ is well defined. Say that $G$ has maximum degree at most $d$ if $\deg_G(x)\le d$ for almost every vertex $x$. Given a measurable partition $I=A\cup B$ (with $A,B$ disjoint Borel sets), a vertex $x\in I$ is said to be $(A,B)$-balanced up to $g$ if $\bigl|\deg_A(x)-\deg_B(x)\bigr|\le g$, where $\deg_A(x)$ and $\deg_B(x)$ count the neighbors of $x$ that lie in $A$ and $B$ respectively.

Determine whether there exists a function $g:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$ with $g(d)=o(d/\log d)$ as $d\to\infty$ such that, for every graphing $G$ of maximum degree at most $d$, there is a measurable partition $I=A\cup B$ for which every vertex $x$ is $(A,B)$-balanced up to $g(d)$.

Related work on hyperfiniteness, local algorithms, and balanced partitions of bounded-degree graphings exists, but no source verifying that the conjectured bound has been proved or disproved was found.

status_evidence.snippet: Foundational results on graphings as limits of bounded-degree graphs; no statement of the specific o(d/log d) balanced partition theorem.
